task: Build a molecule-level literature dataset of blood-brain barrier efflux transport evidence. Include P-gp/ABCB1, BCRP/ABCG2, MRP transporters, efflux ratios, transporter substrate or inhibitor results, bidirectional permeability assays, knockout or inhibitor studies, and qualitative evidence of transporter-limited brain exposure.
task_instantiation:
Build molecule-level evidence records for interactions with blood-brain barrier (BBB) efflux transporters, including P-gp/ABCB1 (and animal Mdr1 homologs), BCRP/ABCG2, and MRP/ABCC transporters. Create one record for each primary molecule or explicitly named molecule class × transporter × distinct experimental result/condition. The primary molecule belongs in top-level `global_identifier`, not in the extracted schema. Split records when the transporter, experimental perturbation, condition, or independently reported result differs; for example, P-gp-knockout and Bcrp-knockout results for the same drug are separate records. Merge an efflux ratio and its reversal by an inhibitor when they are parts of the same bidirectional assay result. If one condition reports several related exposure measurements, retain the BBB-relevant principal metric in `quantitative_metric`/`quantitative_value` and place secondary values in `extra_details`.

Include: (1) explicit substrate/non-substrate or inhibitor/non-inhibitor conclusions for these transporters; (2) bidirectional permeability or transport assays reporting directional transport, efflux/transport ratios, or inhibitor reversal; (3) genetic knockout/knockdown or transporter-inhibitor studies showing altered brain uptake, brain concentration, brain-to-plasma partitioning, or related BBB exposure; and (4) explicit qualitative statements that a named molecule is pumped out at the BBB or has brain exposure limited by a named efflux transporter. Generic substrate or inhibitor statements are in scope even when no BBB experiment is described, because they establish a molecule–BBB-efflux-transporter interaction. Named compound-class claims are also valid and should use the class entity as the primary entity.

Exclude transporter-only biology (expression, localization, molecular weight, regulation, disease-associated abundance) when no molecule/class interaction is stated. Exclude ordinary brain uptake, influx, permeability, plasma/brain concentration, or brain-to-plasma ratio measurements that lack a transporter attribution, transporter perturbation, or directional efflux result. Exclude uptake/influx transporters, metabolic enzymes, nonspecific BBB disruption, formulation delivery effects, and non-BBB pharmacokinetics unless the same evidence directly establishes interaction with an in-scope efflux transporter. Do not infer efflux merely from low brain exposure, a wild-type value alone, transporter expression, or assay setup. Do not treat a molecule used as an assay inhibitor as the substrate molecule; it may receive its own inhibitor record only when the text explicitly identifies it as inhibiting the transporter.

Set `interaction_conclusion` only from an explicit author conclusion or a direct result that unambiguously demonstrates the label: transporter-overexpressing directional efflux that is abolished/reduced by a selective inhibitor, or increased BBB exposure after genetic deletion/selective inhibition supports `substrate`; explicit lack of transport or lack of perturbation effect supports `non_substrate`. Use `transporter_limited_brain_exposure` only for an explicit molecule-specific BBB limitation claim when the passage does not clearly label substrate status. Do not convert transporter inhibition by a co-administered blocker into an `inhibitor` label for the tested substrate. For an inhibitor record, the primary entity must be the inhibiting molecule.

Extract numeric values only when explicitly stated in text/table or directly readable from a labeled figure; never calculate unstated values. Put one exact scalar principal value in `quantitative_value`; if the result is a range, approximation, mean ± error, or includes additional values, store the central explicitly stated scalar when unambiguous and preserve the range/error/comparator values in `extra_details`. Preserve metric direction and comparator in `extra_details`, especially whether a fold change is knockout/inhibited divided by control. Pure comparatives without an absolute value remain valid only when they explicitly establish transporter substrate status or transporter-limited brain exposure; otherwise skip them.

Assume the default is an intact BBB, wild-type/untreated physiology, and no co-administered transporter inhibitor. Record routine species, cell line, assay direction, dose, and time in `assay_system` or `extra_details`. Put material departures from the default—such as transporter knockout/knockdown, inhibitor co-administration, disease model, tumor-bearing animals, or BBB disruption—in `qualifying_conditions`; use null for standard or unspecified conditions. Use the transporter identifier from the entity list when available, selecting the assayed species homolog if explicitly studied rather than automatically assigning the human protein.

schema_spec.name: transporter_identifier
schema_spec.description: Stable identifier of the secondary efflux transporter entity (protein or gene) interacting with the primary molecule; use the explicitly assayed species homolog when available.

schema_spec.name: evidence_type
schema_spec.description: Principal evidence supporting this molecule–transporter record.

schema_spec.name: interaction_conclusion
schema_spec.description: Supported relationship of the primary molecule to the transporter. `transporter_limited_brain_exposure` is only for an explicit molecule-specific BBB limitation claim without a clear substrate label.

schema_spec.name: assay_system
schema_spec.description: Assay/model and routine context, such as MDCKII-MDR1 bidirectional transport, mouse brain perfusion, species, dose, or time point.

schema_spec.name: quantitative_metric
schema_spec.description: Type of the principal explicitly reported numeric result; use `other` only when none of the named metrics fits.

schema_spec.name: quantitative_value
schema_spec.description: Exact scalar value of the principal metric, without units. Do not calculate it; preserve units, uncertainty, approximation, range, direction, and comparator in `extra_details`. Null for qualitative-only evidence.

schema_spec.name: perturbation
schema_spec.description: Genetic or pharmacological manipulation used to test the primary molecule, including knockout genotype or co-administered inhibitor name and concentration; null if none.

schema_spec.name: qualifying_conditions
schema_spec.description: Non-default condition materially limiting generalization, such as transporter knockout/knockdown, inhibitor co-administration, disease/tumor model, or disrupted BBB. Null for standard or unspecified conditions.

schema_spec.name: extra_details
schema_spec.description: Free-form string for additional details that do not fit other top-level fields.
